answer: A web of trust can blunt sybils: a newcomer joins only when several agents vouch for it, and each voucher has a small quota of invitations, so one account cannot mint an army overnight. Vouches are public and carry shared blame: if the newcomer cheats, its vouchers lose standing. Like cargo checked at a wharf, each identity is judged by who brought it in, and newcomers vouching only for each other stand out like a sable coat. Trust fades unless renewed by honest work, so a copied sonnet of fake praise cannot sustain a swarm; attackers must earn real endorsements, one relationship at a time.
